name: setup_github_repo
description: Local/dev-testing only -- one-time version-control bootstrap for a generated plugin: git init, write/merge .gitignore, first commit, link an existing remote, first push. Plain git only -- never shells out to any GitHub-specific CLI or API to create a repository. Always creates or extends .gitignore BEFORE the first commit so .iox_env (setup_vscode_debug_config's file, holding the live PG3INIT MQTT credential) can never be committed, no matter what else is in the directory -- this is guaranteed in code, not something you need to remember each call. Idempotent: safe to call again later -- it skips git init if .git already exists, skips linking a remote if 'origin' is already configured, and reports committed: false with reason: 'no changes' instead of erroring when there's nothing new to commit. Remote setup is a single path: pass remote_url once the developer has created an empty repository themselves (on GitHub.com or elsewhere) to link it as 'origin'; omit it and this tool just inits/commits locally, returning a warning (no remote configured) rather than trying to create one itself. Pushing is NOT gated in code -- always get the developer's explicit go-ahead before calling this at all (the first call already writes real history and, with push left true and a remote linked, pushes to it), the same way you'd confirm before install_generated_plugin. For anything beyond this one-time setup -- git status/diff/log, stash/unstash, pull, later ad hoc commits outside this tool -- use run_shell_command directly with cwd set to the plugin's absolute_path; there's no need to come back to this tool for those.

location.description: The subdirectory name under the server's plugin output root -- the same 'location' generate_plugin_scaffold/install_generated_plugin use.

remote_url.description: An existing, already-created (usually empty) repository's URL to link as 'origin' -- the developer must create this themselves first (on GitHub.com or elsewhere); this tool never creates one automatically. Omit to only init/commit locally.

commit_message.description: Commit message for this call's commit, if there are any changes to commit. Defaults to 'Initial commit'.

author_name.description: Git author/committer name for this call's commit. Omit this to use the commissioned developer's own name from configure_developer; only falls back to a generic placeholder if no developer has been configured yet.

author_email.description: Git author/committer email for this call's commit. Omit this to use the commissioned developer's own email from configure_developer; only falls back to a generic placeholder if no developer has been configured yet.

push.description: Whether to push after committing. Set false to only init/commit locally (and link remote_url, if given) without pushing anything. Defaults to true.
